_: RULE-2026-11-13-E. The plugins and MCP servers each headless job class loads, decided by Sana 2026-11-13. Read by the launchers once ASK-4756 wires them; pinned by q-system/.q-system/tests/test_fleet_load_allowlist.py. No job class loads account connectors.
measured: 2026-11-12/13 (token-drain analysis section 3, ASK-4756): every agent loads a skill listing of about 7.7k tokens and about 500 deferred MCP tool names, about 8.6k tokens, re-read on every request. 309 skill entries across 24 user-scope plugins: 164 from one analytics plugin (161 SKILL.md files in its cache), 38 from the fleet's own.

worker.why: A builder works through these plugins' hooks: fable-discipline-lint (prd-os), rca-lint (kipi-core), the issue hooks (kipi-dsse), the dogfood gate and design door (kipi-design). It reaches Linear and GitHub through scripts, so it needs no MCP server. kipi-ops (one interpretive skill, no hooks) and kipi-notebooklm (a research MCP server) serve no build step. Its plugins' own MCP servers (kipi-core ships one) stay off: strict_mcp means the launcher passes a strict, empty MCP config.

startup_ceiling.measured: 2026-11-12/13, one claude -p in a kipi-system tree with this row applied (ASK-4756): first request 76,036 tokens, 76,166 re-measured after the account sync below (117,872 with the full set: 345 skills, 617 deferred tool names, 37 MCP servers). Post-trim counts: 13 deferred tool names, 0 MCP servers, 121 skills. The skill count was 106 until an account sync on 2026-11-13 added 4 @synced plugins (now turned off here) and 15 anthropic-skills:* account skills, which no enabledPlugins key reaches.
startup_ceiling.why: A ratchet, not a cap on runs: fleet_load.py startup reads each worker run's transcript and alerts Sana once when a count crosses this line. The margin (about 15% on skills, 7 tool names) lets a few new skills land without an alert; a new plugin or any MCP server does not. The listing's text is capped by the CLI near 30k characters at 106, 121 and 345 skills, so the count is the measure, not the characters.

review.why: A reviewer reads the PR tree and writes one verdict file. Plugin hooks guard writes it does not make, and it reads any rule it cites from the PR tree with Read or Grep: the lean reviewer loads no CLAUDE.md, rules or settings at start (ASK-4743).

background.why: lean_call.py already runs with no settings, no tools and an empty strict MCP config. This row records that as the decision.

interactive.why: The four largest non-fleet plugins (164, 42, 19 and 13 entries) leave user scope. Each stays installed at project scope where a session used it in the last 30 days; ASK-4756 measures that from transcripts before the move. The fleet's own plugins stay user scope: a plugin scoped to one project loses its slash commands in every other project.
